I don't actually feel this way, even though I know it's statistically true. it's more like there is a large cluster at the middle that is indistinguishable – slightly above average and slightly below average look just about the same, and since most people have one or more things they're particularly good at, anyone can appear above average in the right situation.

Put me in the World Snooker Championship and I'm going to look mighty stupid. I know how the game is played, how it's scored, and what skills are required to be good at it. That doesn't mean I actually possess any ability. Take one of those players and ask him to write a song, chances are he's going to suck at it, even if he can objectively define what good music sounds like. (There are probably a handful that could sit down and write a song, just because musical talent isn't all that rare.) In that case, I'm going to look a lot smarter.

The world is largely designed for average people. Being close to average is generally good enough, it just takes a bit longer to learn how to get by. That's why you won't notice that half the population is below average. They've already learned to compensate for it.

It's the outliers, on both ends, that are going to stand out. Even then, you get stupid people who are particularly good at something, and smart people who totally fail it.
